userText:
Building: Palace of Fine Arts (rotunda and colonnades), San Francisco (exhibition rotunda).
The front (−z) is the lagoon side of the rotunda.
Footprint: 72.9 m along x by 68.1 m along z, centred on the origin.
Outline (from OpenStreetMap), [x, z] in metres, going round:
[[30.8,4.7],[36.4,8.8],[19.8,10.8],[14.5,17.2],[16.1,34],[6.5,21.7],[-7.9,28.4],[-17.1,14.7],[-20,19],[-25.2,15.2],[-22.6,-1.8],[-36.4,-8.7],[-25.7,-8.4],[-14.7,-17.2],[-16.1,-33.9],[-6.2,-21.8],[1.7,-22.5],[4.8,-34],[16.7,-14.7],[27.8,-17],[32.4,-11.4],[21.7,-6.1],[22.3,2.2]]
Height: the highest point is 49 m above the ground.
Model the rotunda only: the long curving colonnades that run off on either side are outside this footprint.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. front view across the lagoon of the domed rotunda and flanking curved colonnades, daylight
  2. three-quarter from the lawn across the lagoon showing the rotunda, colonnade at left and trees, daylight
  3. view from the Marina side showing the rotunda dome and the long hall behind it, houses in front, daylight

Reply with the JSON object only.


Three differences stand out. The dome is too tall and narrow, so it reads as an egg where the real one is a broad, low hemisphere. The base is a square slab, while the real rotunda stands on a round stone platform. The columns are thin and dark, and the great arches between the piers do not read clearly, so the ring looks like free columns.
